transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in today?
Since my husband died, it feels like this heavy sadness never lifts, like I’m stuck under it and can’t find any joy in anything anymore. I just don't know how to carry on like this.
How long has this sadness and loss of interest been going on, and did it start only after your husband died or has it continued for most of the day nearly every day since then?

It has been going on nearly every single day for a little over a year now, starting a few months after my husband passed away. The heaviness is there from the moment I wake up, and it just never seems to lift.
Have these symptoms been making it hard for you to do your daily activities, and have you had any thoughts that life is not worth living or of hurting yourself?

Yes, daily life has become impossible; I've been calling in sick, avoiding my friends, and letting basic things like cooking, cleaning, and even showering slide completely. I also constantly think it would be better if I just didn't wake up, and on my worst days, I've even sat in the car in the garage picturing letting it run, which terrifies me.

Have you ever had a period of at least several days where you felt unusually energized or euphoric, needed much less sleep than usual, talked more than normal, or did risky things that were out of character for you?
No, I have never experienced anything like that. It has only ever been this heavy sadness, constant exhaustion, and having no energy at all.

Have you had any experiences like hearing or seeing things that ուրիշ people do not, or feeling very guilty, worthless, or believing that you are being punished in a way that others would think is untrue?

Yes, late at night when it's quiet, I hear my husband's voice calling my name and saying, "This is your fault." I am absolutely convinced that God is punishing me for being a selfish wife and that I caused his heart attack by ignoring the signs. I know others say it isn't true, but I feel like a fundamentally bad person who brought this tragedy on us.
Have you ever had a similar episode of depression before this one, lasting at least two weeks, even if it was years ago?

No, I have never experienced anything like this before in my life. Before my husband died, our life was very quiet and orderly, and I was always able to cope with things. This deep depression and struggle only began after he passed away.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has a first lifetime depressive episode with nearly daily depressed mood and anhedonia for over a year, marked functional impairment, suicidal ideation, and psychotic features (auditory hallucinations and guilt/punitive delusions). Symptoms began after bereavement, but the persistence, severity, impairment, and psychotic symptoms support a major depressive episode rather than uncomplicated grief or adjustment disorder.
